q: What is 'pét-nat' shorthand for, and its method?
accept: petillant naturel ancestral method
one fermentation bottled before finished
ans: Pétillant naturel — méthode ancestrale: bottled mid-fermentation, one ferment only
exp: Crown caps, often undisgorged; Limoux and Bugey-Cerdon are the ancestral homelands.

cloudy bottle-fermented refermented sui lieviti

q: Franciacorta Satèn is defined by which pair of rules?
opts: White grapes only, at no more than 5 atmospheres
Pinot Nero only, bottled at a minimum of 6 atmospheres
Chardonnay only, aged a minimum of 60 months on lees
Rosé only, with dosage of at least 17 grams per litre
exp: Satèn is Franciacorta's own invented style, not an EU category. It must be white-grape only — Chardonnay with up to 50% Pinot Bianco, never Pinot Nero — bottled at a maximum 5 atmospheres for a softer, silkier mousse, held 24 months minimum on the lees, and released only in the Brut typology, under 12 g/L: there is no legal Satèn Extra Brut or Pas Dosé. The lower pressure comes from dosing less tirage sugar, not from degassing: about 4 g/L of sugar buys roughly one atmosphere, so Satèn takes around 20 g/L instead of 24.

q: Cava's 2022 restructuring split the DO into which two quality bands, and what lees minimums sit inside the upper one?
accept: cava de guarda nine months and guarda superior reserva 18 gran reserva 30 paraje 36
de guarda and de guarda superior with reserva gran reserva and paraje calificado
guarda superior holds reserva eighteen gran reserva thirty paraje calificado thirty-six
two bands guarda at 9 months and guarda superior from 18 to 36 months
ans: Cava de Guarda (minimum 9 months) and Cava de Guarda Superior — inside it Reserva at 18 months, Gran Reserva at 30, and Cava de Paraje Calificado at 36
exp: The reform was Cava's answer to Corpinnat's exit and to its own reputation for cheap volume. Everything in the Guarda Superior band must be vintage-dated, from vines at least ten years old, and organically certified — mandatory from the 2025 harvest. The same reform mapped production zones: Comtats de Barcelona, Valle del Ebro, Viñedos de Almendralejo and Zona de Levante. Learn the ladder as 9 / 18 / 30 / 36 and you can place any Cava on sight.

q: Prosecco DOC Rosé, legal only since 2020, requires which second grape, in what proportion and vinified how — and what else is compulsory on the label?
accept: pinot nero 10 to 15 percent vinified as red with glera at 85 and a compulsory vintage
glera minimum 85 percent plus pinot nero vinified in rosso vintage mandatory
pinot noir ten to fifteen percent red vinification and the year on the label
pinot nero for colour at 10-15% and it must be millesimato
ans: Pinot Nero at 10–15%, vinified in rosso to supply the colour, with Glera at a minimum 85% — and the vintage must be stated
exp: Note that the Pinot Nero is vinified in rosso — it is the colour source, not a seasoning, which is the opposite of its role in white Prosecco DOC blends. The wine is spumante only (no frizzante), spends at least 60 days in tank on the second fermentation, and is always millesimato: the compulsory vintage was the concession that made a pink Prosecco acceptable to a consortium that had spent thirty years insisting Prosecco was white.

q: Distinguish Blanquette de Limoux from Crémant de Limoux by grape, and state what Blanquette Méthode Ancestrale must be.
accept: blanquette is 90 percent mauzac cremant is chardonnay led ancestrale is pure mauzac
mauzac dominates blanquette chardonnay dominates cremant ancestral is all mauzac
at least 90% mauzac versus a chardonnay based cremant and a single ferment mauzac ancestral
blanquette mauzac cremant chardonnay and chenin ancestrale 100% mauzac single fermentation
ans: Blanquette is at least 90% Mauzac; Crémant is Chardonnay-led with Chenin Blanc in support; Méthode Ancestrale is 100% Mauzac, one fermentation only, low in alcohol and off-dry
exp: The three appellations are a grape ladder from tradition to international polish, and Limoux's claim to the first sparkling wine — Saint-Hilaire, 1531 — rests on Mauzac. Mauzac's marker is bruised apple and apple skin: taste that in a blind southern French fizz and say Blanquette. The ancestral version stops at roughly 6–7% alcohol because the single fermentation is arrested by cold, leaving sugar and a gentle pressure.

q: Under EU labelling law, a sparkling wine marked Extra Dry contains how much residual sugar?
exp: 12–17 g/L. The full scale: brut nature 0–3 with no added dosage, extra brut 0–6, brut under 12, extra dry 12–17, sec/dry 17–32, demi-sec 32–50, doux above 50 — with a ±3 g/L analytical tolerance and deliberate overlaps between bands. Extra Dry is the category that catches guests and candidates alike: it is sweeter than Brut despite sounding drier, and it is the default style of Prosecco.

q: South Africa's traditional-method category recently shortened its name. From what to what, and what does the category legally require?
accept: methode cap classique shortened to cap classique bottle fermented twelve months on lees
dropped the word methode leaving cap classique second ferment in bottle 12 months
name is now cap classique alone requiring bottle fermentation and a year on the lees
from methode cap classique to cap classique with 12 months minimum lees ageing
ans: 'Méthode Cap Classique' became simply 'Cap Classique' — a second fermentation in the bottle in which the wine is sold, with a minimum twelve months on the lees
exp: The producers dropped 'Méthode' to stop borrowing French vocabulary and to build a name South Africa owns outright — the same instinct that produced Cap Classique in the first place. Simonsig's 1971 Kaapse Vonkel is the category's zero point, and the Cape's cool-site plantings in Elgin, Robertson's limestone and the Hemel-en-Aarde now supply most of the serious fruit. On the floor, never call it Champagne method: call it Cap Classique.

q: Alta Langa DOCG's rules set it apart from every other Italian traditional-method zone in three ways. Name them.
accept: pinot nero and chardonnay only always vintage dated thirty months on the lees
only pinot nero or chardonnay with a compulsory vintage and 30 months minimum
vintage is mandatory grapes are pinot nero chardonnay and lees ageing is 30 months
pinot nero chardonnay 90 percent millesimato always riserva at 36 months
ans: Pinot Nero and/or Chardonnay only, a minimum 90% of the blend; the vintage is always compulsory; and a minimum 30 months on the lees, rising to 36 for Riserva
exp: Piedmont's serious fizz — DOCG since 2011, planted above 250 metres across Alessandria, Asti and Cuneo. The compulsory vintage is the detail to hold: no other major Italian metodo classico forces it. The appellation exists because Piedmont's houses spent a century growing Pinot Nero base wine for other people's bottles and finally claimed a name of their own.
